SHARED DESIGN LANGUAGE: tokens navy-950 #060a14 / brand-500 #6f47f5 / brand-400 #8a70fb / accent-blue #3b82f6 / accent-cyan #22d3ee, Geist, `grad-text`, `.card`, `.btn-primary`/`.btn-deploy`, `hero-aura`, glass + violet glow; cyan = "live" pop, never amber except warnings. Real product-screens as centerpiece; asymmetric/editorial layouts (NOT centered-stack); animated "live" elements; compact 5-star review element; "47 seconds away" speed hook; buying-psychology focus; LESS text MORE presentation. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`; mobile-responsive (390w). FORBIDDEN (rejected slop): centered-stack→particle-canvas→3-up-grid skeleton; fake globes; dead-space cards; text walls. Reusable showcase components in `components/marketing/showcase/` — especially `ClaudeChat` and any ClaudeBuilder — plus `DeployCard`, `MatrixTerminal`, `NetworkMap`. Reuse/evolve them.

**Template 1 — AI / vibe-coding hosting (`/preview/ai-hosting`, component under `components/marketing/aihostingtemplate/`):** this is Nxeon's BIGGEST growth area — a Claude-powered "Build with AI" builder that also hosts. Hero centerpiece: an animated **"describe it → AI builds it → deploys in 47s"** flow (evolve `ClaudeChat`/ClaudeBuilder showcase — a chat prompt typing, then a build/deploy sequence). Add the **"already built it elsewhere? import & host your Bolt / Lovable / v0 / Cursor app"** angle (a key wedge). Include a deploy terminal moment, plan cards, and compact reviews. This should feel like the most modern, exciting page on the site.

**Template 2 — Shared web hosting (`/preview/web-hosting`, component under `components/marketing/webhostingtemplate/`):** WordPress/one-click managed hosting. Hero: an animated "site live in seconds" element (a browser/site frame populating, or a one-click WordPress install animating). Add cPanel-class feature showcase, honest flat-pricing plan cards (lean into "no renewal price hikes" — a real trust wedge from the SERPs), a free-migration CTA, compact reviews, the 47s hook.

CONCURRENCY CONSTRAINTS (7 agents share this tree): NET-NEW files only; do NOT touch existing live pages/shared components/MarketingHeader/GameLandingPage (READ OK). **Do NOT edit `app/globals.css`** — use co-located CSS Modules (`*.module.css`) or inline; REUSE existing `pv-*` keyframes. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Do NOT run `npm run build` and do NOT run a dev server / screenshots (main session does one pass). Report the 2 route paths + concerns.

I have what I need on the design tokens, approved game-landing patterns, showcase components, and pricing conventions, plus the preview route structure. Now I'm ready to design the two templates, starting with the AI hosting preview page.

The web-hosting preview lives at a nested route so it won't collide with the existing live page, and both need to be net-new files without touching globals.css—reusing the existing pv-* keyframes instead. Since these are client-side animated components, I'm weighing whether to reuse hooks like usePrefersReducedMotion and useCountUp from the gamelanding kit or build a separate local kit to avoid cross-folder dependencies.

I'll go with separate folders for each template, each containing its own component, data, and hooks files, and reuse the gamelanding kit's hooks (usePrefersReducedMotion, useInViewOnce, useCountUp, useTypedLines, useJitter) via import since it's a preview kit meant for reuse rather than a locked shared component like the header.

On reflection, I'll prioritize isolation over DRY: rather than importing from gamelanding/kit, I'll create a small net-new hooks file local to each template folder with just the needed hooks. It's a bit of duplication, but it guarantees my work stays unaffected by whatever other agents do to shared files.

Now I want to design each template's layout and content so they're distinct from the three game directions and from each other. For the AI/vibe-coding hosting template, I'm thinking of a bold, modern "Build with AI" concept centered around Claude-powered building tools.

The signature hero would be an asymmetric layout with a headline and "describe it, ship it in 47s" hook on the left, and a large animated Build Console on the right showing a multi-stage sequence: a chat prompt typing, Claude streaming build steps that check off one by one, a deploy terminal line, and finally a live browser preview rendering the finished site. I want this to feel like a single continuous, evolving component that captures the whole build-to-deploy flow in motion.

Below that I'm sketching an "import wedge" section for users who already built something on Bolt, Lovable, v0, or Cursor -- a row of source wordmark chips paired with an animated import flow showing detection of the framework and deployment, plus its own terminal moment running something like an import command that detects the stack, builds it, and goes live. Then a feature bento explaining why to host on Nxeon (full server control, visibility into every step, approval gates, instant HTTPS, VPS scaling), followed by honest pricing plan cards built around build credits and hosting tiers.

I'm keeping the pricing qualitative and plausible rather than inventing specific credit numbers, using tiers like Starter/Pro/Scale with features like AI build sessions, custom domains, and always-on hosting, then closing with compact starred reviews and a final CTA line about going live in 47 seconds. The overall motion signature -- typing chat, streaming build steps, an assembling browser preview, and the import flow -- is what sets this apart from more game-like interfaces.

Now I'm sketching Template 2, a shared web hosting concept centered on WordPress-style one-click installs, emphasizing trust, speed, and no renewal price hikes. The hero animation shows a progress sequence from installing WordPress through configuring the database and issuing SSL to a live site, paired with a browser frame, headline, trust chips like free SSL and free migration, and star ratings in an asymmetric editorial layout distinct from the other templates.

I'm adding a "no renewal price hikes" trust section with an animated price-over-time chart comparing competitors spiking at renewal versus Nxeon staying flat, plus a cPanel-style feature grid mockup showing file manager, databases, email, one-click apps, and SSL controls.

Rounding out the page with a one-click apps row, honest flat-pricing tier cards, a free-migration CTA with a mini migration flow visual, and compact reviews before the final CTA — each section's motion signature staying distinct (install progress, site assembly, price bars, panel tiles) while keeping everything mobile-responsive at 390px, respecting reduced-motion preferences, and type-checking cleanly. These will be client components given the animation load.

For reviews, I'll build a small local star-rating row rather than pulling from a shared kit, keeping the component self-contained. I also need to hold to the honesty guardrails: 24/7 means monitoring not live support, never fabricate server counts or locations, AI-build flows must show an approval gate, migration must distinguish handled versus flagged items, and Nxeon speaks in first-person as the owner rather than third-party provider language, avoiding the word "provider" entirely.

Reviews should stay modest and illustrative, consistent with how the existing testimonials are handled without added disclaimers. I'll thread the approve-gate idea into the AI build flow copy ("review and approve before it ships") to keep things honest, then move to planning the file structure -- starting with a hooks file for the AI hosting template that includes reduced-motion detection, in-view triggers, typing animation, staged sequence reveals, and the star row component.
